Title: Prosed | Go from newsletters & podcasts to published manuscript | Product Hunt
# Prosed. ### Your newsletter archive owes you a book. I did some math recently that kind of blew my mind. If you've published a weekly newsletter for 3 years, you've written roughly 150,000 words. ### Trending products. I never thought of writing a book myself before, but between my blog posts, workshops, patents, and publications, this is very intriguing! Especially if it can do it in my voice. Between blog posts, workshops, patents, and publications, you've got more than enough for a book. They just never had time to sit down and connect the dots, or how I like to say, **give it a spine!**. That's exactly what Prosed does. Prosed analyzes your existing writing to capture how you actually sound. The result reads like you wrote it, because it's built from your actual content. How much content would you need to get a solid output from your perspective? For a solid book, you'd want around 30-50+ pieces of content. Your social posts are great for voice fingerprinting and filling gaps, and podcast appearances work well, especially if you're doing most of the talking in them. The real question is how much of that content circles around a consistent theme. When you upload your content we tell you roughly how many books it's worth :). **4** LinkedIn posts and social threads are great for voice fingerprinting and filling gaps, but hard to build a full book from those alone. If you write about productivity one week and crypto the next and parenting the next, that's where it gets harder, and the post's first draft back and forth becomes important. For a book workflow, I’d love a source-to-chapter map: which passages came from the creator’s original material, which connective tissue Prosed added, and where the author marked “not me” or “not my point.” That would make the manuscript feel less like an AI rewrite and more like an editable spine for the body of work they already built. Think creators who already have a lot of content out there (newsletters, podcasts, courses, guides), and want to assemble that into a book.
